memory_update.text: COUR should be treated as the main public pure-play after the May 11, 2026 Coursera-Udemy combination; UDMY should no longer be modeled as a standalone US-listed candidate.
DCBO is below the preferred USD 1B market-cap threshold but is unusually relevant because it owns enterprise LMS infrastructure, ARR, subscription revenue, and extended-enterprise learning workflows.

SKIL is a high-specificity but high-risk below-USD-1B exception; its node relevance is strong, but listing compliance, leverage, and revenue trajectory require evidence checks before any quality ranking.

For this node, HCM system-of-record companies such as WDAY and SAP may be more important chokepoint owners than many education-content providers because they control skills taxonomy, completion records, compliance auditability, and HR workflow integration.

Microsoft/LinkedIn Learning and Viva Learning are important obvious leaders for a later platform/integration pass, but were excluded from the five-name cap here because Microsoft has much broader revenue exposure and lower node purity than COUR, DCBO, SKIL, WDAY, and SAP.
COUR should now be treated as the combined Coursera-Udemy public vehicle after the May 11, 2026 closing, not as a standalone Coursera-only platform.
UDMY should generally be removed as a standalone active candidate after the merger closing; keep historical Udemy Business metrics as segment evidence for COUR integration work.

For enterprise workforce upskilling, the chokepoint appears to be shifting from raw course inventory to skills taxonomy, HRIS/workflow integration, trusted content, enterprise retention, and auditable outcomes.
WDAY and MSFT are second-order but strategically important because they control employee systems of record, skills graphs, workplace distribution, and AI productivity workflows.

Need a separate pass on private or non-US-listed learning infrastructure vendors such as Cornerstone, Degreed, 360Learning, Pluralsight, SAP SuccessFactors, and Absorb, because several important chokepoint assets may not map cleanly to US-listed pure plays.
Use COUR, not UDMY, for public-market exposure to the combined Coursera/Udemy skills platform after the May 11, 2026 closing.
Enterprise upskilling exposure is split between content/platform vendors such as COUR and DCBO and workflow/system-of-record chokepoints such as WDAY and ADP.

DCBO is below the preferred USD 1B market-cap threshold based on recent market-cap indications, but it remains a high-relevance exception because it is a direct enterprise learning and skills-intelligence platform.

LRN is a weaker but useful adjacent candidate: the exposure is not pure enterprise LMS, but healthcare, IT, adult career training, and workforce-board/employer-sponsored cohorts make it relevant to workforce reskilling.

Private or non-US-listed leaders such as Cornerstone OnDemand, Skillsoft-related assets, Guild, Degreed, Pluralsight, and LinkedIn Learning/Microsoft require separate mapping because they influence the competitive landscape but may not offer clean standalone US-listed exposure.

node: Enterprise workforce upskilling and corporate e-learning platforms
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Expanded the direct and near-direct US-listed universe for enterprise workforce upskilling. The strongest direct public exposure is the newly combined Coursera/Udemy platform, followed by Docebo and Skillsoft as pure-play or near-pure-play enterprise learning vendors. Workday and SAP are included as second-order but strategically important HR/HCM system-of-record platforms because the bottleneck hypothesis emphasizes workflow integration, skills taxonomy, compliance tracking, and measurable workforce outcomes rather than simple course supply. Microsoft/LinkedIn Learning is a notable coverage gap for a later broader platform pass, but was excluded here to keep the universe to five names and prioritize higher node specificity. Expanded the universe around the enterprise workforce upskilling node with emphasis on scarce or constrained capabilities: enterprise distribution, HR/workflow integrations, skills taxonomy, trusted AI/compliance/technical content, and measurable learning-to-work outcomes. The best-fit public candidates are not only pure-play course platforms; the chokepoint increasingly sits in systems of record such as HRIS, skills graphs, workflow platforms, and enterprise knowledge/data layers that can connect learning to roles, performance, compliance, and productivity. Expanded universe for the enterprise workforce upskilling node, emphasizing second-order beneficiaries where the chokepoint may be distribution through enterprise HR systems, skills intelligence, compliance workflows, measurable outcomes, and trusted AI-era content rather than generic course supply.
